newsitem.title: USA: U.S. nominee Eizenstat to stress free trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. nominee Eizenstat to stress free trade.

text.p: Stuart Eizenstat said Thursday he would focus on removing trade barriers if he was confirmed as undersecretary of State for Economic, Business and Agricultural Affairs.
"Trade has to be more of a two-way street," he said at his Senate Foreign Relations Committee confirmation hearing.
"Our economic health depends considerably on our ability to have access to markets abroad," he added.
Eizenstat said economic issues were becoming an increasingly important element of U.S. foreign policy after national security and political concerns.
Sen. Jesse Helms, R-N.C., urged Eizenstat to stress the issue of confiscated U.S. property in Cuba during negotiations with the European Union over trade restrictions on Cuba.
Helms is co-author of a law that imposes U.S. sanctions on foreign companies that do business with Cuba. Eizenstat negotiated an agreement with the EU to seek to soften the law.
Eizenstat expressed concern over an agreement by France to invest in Cuba, but did not suggest any U.S. response.
He has served as undersecretary of Commerce and U.S. ambassador to the EU and was a senior aide in President Jimmy Carter's administration.
